articles.body: Part 29 · One Agent, Five Platforms An agent card is a CV for an agent. It tells other agents who it is, what it can do, where to reach it and how to prove who's calling. And like a CV, what you leave off matters as much as what you put on. Part 28 had the supplier-communication agent on Azure read the invoice agent's card before asking about invoice 4471. This part writes both cards. It's based on the A2A 1.0 specification as I read it on 17 November 2026. The cards are illustrative, for the series' fictional company, and nothing here has been deployed. What a card has to contain The specification defines the card as a "self-describing manifest for an agent". Eight fields are required: name and description: for people and for other agents.

articles.title: Keep CSS scroll snap targets visible below a fixed header
articles.excerpt: A scroll-snap layout can select the correct section and still feel broken: the section heading lands beneath a fixed header. The snap rule is not necessarily wrong. The scrolling container simply has…
articles.body: A scroll-snap layout can select the correct section and still feel broken: the section heading lands beneath a fixed header. The snap rule is not necessarily wrong. The scrolling container simply has no knowledge that part of the visible area is occupied by persistent chrome. The implementation decision is to reserve that shared space on the scroll container with scroll-padding-top , using the fixed header’s height. This changes the container’s effective snapport: when a section snaps to start , the browser treats the area below the header as the useful top edge. The section can retain its existing scroll-snap-align: start , and the container can retain mandatory vertical snapping. That separation matters.

articles.title: Shopify's image_tag already lazy-loads. Here's what it leaves to you.
articles.excerpt: I used to write my own lazy-loading logic in every Shopify theme. Then I read the image_tag docs properly and deleted most of it. Shopify already does more than people think, and the two things it doe…
articles.body: I used to write my own lazy-loading logic in every Shopify theme. Then I read the image_tag docs properly and deleted most of it. Shopify already does more than people think, and the two things it doesn't do are the ones that actually move LCP. Here's what you get for free, what you still have to write, and a hero snippet I now paste into most theme builds. What image_tag does on its own {{ product . featured_image | image_url : width : 1200 | image_tag }} That one line gives you: width and height attributes , taken from the image's dimensions. No layout shift as the image loads. A srcset with a set of widths Shopify picks, up to the width you asked for in image_url . loading="lazy" on images in sections further down the page. A modern format.

articles.body: On November 10, Chrome shipped Modern Web Guidance 1.0 , and the project is now stewarded by Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and MDN together. On X it got passed around as "the thing that fixes AI coding habits", usually right next to the other running complaint of the week: vibe-coded sites all look the same, and they all ship the same 2019-era front-end code underneath. The pitch is simple. Coding agents can make almost anything work with JavaScript, but a web platform expert reviewing that code can usually find a native HTML or CSS feature that does the job with less code, better accessibility, and better performance. Modern Web Guidance packages that expertise as skills your agent can search, plus a static scanner called legacy-scan .

articles.title: When a MeowShield-protected build breaks, lower the level and re-enable options one at a time
articles.excerpt: A JavaScript protection pass can fail in unhelpful ways. The output looks fine in the workspace, then a Safari tab throws, a Node.js CLI exits at startup, or a host page can no longer find a function…
articles.body: A JavaScript protection pass can fail in unhelpful ways. The output looks fine in the workspace, then a Safari tab throws, a Node.js CLI exits at startup, or a host page can no longer find a function it used to call. The worst next step is to enable more options, or jump to a stronger preset, in the hope that a heavier transform will just work. MeowShield's official troubleshooting advice is the opposite. If protected code no longer works, lower the protection level or disable some options, then add options back one at a time and re-test. I help promote MeowShield. This article turns that advice into a loop you can finish without guessing. Freeze the experiment Before you change anything else, save the exact inputs that failed: The original source, under your own backup.

articles.title: Review an AI CAD Sketch Before Adding It to a Project Brief
articles.excerpt: A concept sketch can help a developer or designer explain a physical idea, but a polished rendering can also conceal unanswered questions. Suppose you are adding a small sensor enclosure to a project…
articles.body: A concept sketch can help a developer or designer explain a physical idea, but a polished rendering can also conceal unanswered questions. Suppose you are adding a small sensor enclosure to a project brief. The team needs to discuss the location of its opening, the available mounting space, and the dimensions that came from the brief. Review the sketch as an input to that discussion and attach the questions someone needs to resolve in the next version. Separate the brief from the generated details Write the required outer dimensions, units, and openings in a short reference note. Identify where each value came from. A sensor board specification might establish one dimension, while the enclosure depth is still a proposal. Keep those distinctions visible before comparing the sketch.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 just reached a light-day in space, but Voyager 2 won't do the same until 2035, due to speed choices made throughout their 50-year missions.
articles.body: Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer?

The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries.

articles.title: Space is filling up with junk. Could laser-reflecting mirrors help humanity clean things up?
articles.excerpt: The British company Foundational thinks its laser-reflecting tech can help humanity fight the space-junk problem — and it just proved out a demo version in an orbital test.
articles.body: A British startup thinks it can help humanity deal with its space junk problem. Millions of pieces of space debris circle Earth at the moment, according to the European Space Agency (ESA). Even the smallest fragments are potentially dangerous, given how fast stuff travels in orbit. Experts have proposed a range of measures to deal with this junk. The smallest bits, for example, may require big space nets, or lasering the stuff down to Earth. Large satellites are increasingly being deliberately deorbited these days, and a few have even been refueled to keep them operating in orbit — something that will likely start happening more and more over the coming years. Now, the British startup Foundational has another idea to throw into the mix: retroreflectors.

articles.body: 4 Min Read New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra A new album from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory collects snapshots of baby stars across the galaxy and beyond and transforms that data into sound. Four new sonifications use data of stars that are actively forming, captured by Chandra and other NASA telescopes By studying places in the universe where stars are currently being born and young stars are present, astronomers can better understand the lifecycle of all stars, including our own Sun. articles.body: We're in a bit of a cyberpunk revival at the moment. 2026 gave the excellent second season of Netflix’s "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners," and Prime Video's " Blade Runner 2099 " is just around the corner. 2027 will continue this trend with " Neuromancer " blasting onto Apple TV. Based on cyberspace guru William Gibson’s seminal 1984 novel, "Neuromancer" follows Case, a brilliant hacker who falls into a web of digital espionage and crime as he attempts an impossible corporate heist. The pulp noir novel has been hailed as a generational revelation, and its slang and terminology have become ingrained in computer nerd subcultures.
